60071801.text: The Wild Hunt assault on Starsand Shoal, you mean? Huge wave. First I've ever seen of that size. Good thing it was so brief.

60071802.text: No, no, I mean there's been another, to the north of Nasha Town.

60071803.text: What? How many does that make in the last couple of days now? What are the Lightkeepers playing at...

60071804.text: Can't be helped. There were only a handful stationed on our side in the first place, and the cannon hasn't been fixed yet either. They've been strained to breaking point for a while now, I'll bet.

60071805.text: *sigh* I'm bugging out if this goes on much longer. And here you all told me this was a good place to do business... Fool me once, I say!

60071806.text: Hey now, this could be our big break! My second-eldest brother made his fortune off Wild Hunt attacks, you know. C'mon, let's get moving. There won't be anything left for us if we're late.

60071807.text: Left for us to... scavenge? Mm... I did hear about an overturned cargo vehicle over there...

60071810.text: Huh... Should've told them that those are dangerous thoughts.

60071813.text: Guess you're right. Even if we solved this Wild Hunt problem, they'd probably just jump head-first into some new danger if they thought they could earn some quick Mora...

60071814.text: Some self-reflection might not be unwarranted, y'know...

60071815.text: Hmph... Paimon'll have you know that when it comes to staying outta trouble, greed and cowardice make the perfect match!

60071816.text: Should you really be proud of that...

60071817.text: (Still, the Wild Hunt's been getting wilder ever since we foiled that mysterious phantom's plan at Starsand Shoal.)

60071818.text: (The two of them seem closely connected, and that phantom may very well attack again... even though we know almost nothing about it.)

60071819.text: (...In fact, where would we even begin with such an investigation?)

60071820.text: Hey, look — Aino and Ineffa are here in Nasha Town. Ooh, considering what those people said earlier, d'you think they're here to fix that cannon up?

60071822.text: Hehe, dying to know something, aren't ya? You totally zoned out just now...

60070101.text: #Ah. Familiar faces identified — our good friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

60070103.text: Those evaluations could not be more different!

60070104.text: Might I ask who this is?

60070105.text: This is Sousi, Sergeant Major of the nearby Lightkeepers. He's stationed here in this town.

60070107.text: He is Flins's superior, as far as position is considered.

60070108.text: A pleasure to meet you all.

60070109.text: #This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon, friends of ours. They're experienced adventurers who are new to Nod-Krai.

60070111.text: Pleased to meet you. Were you talking about the cannon, by any chance?

60070112.text: Indeed. The sooner we can get it firing again, the quicker we can ease our current... predicament.

60070113.text: Two more Wild Hunt incursions have come sweeping in at different locations after the last one at Starsand Shoal. Our manpower is already stretched, as it is — this is more than we can handle.

60070114.text: Hasn't Flins gone back to your HQ to ask for reinforcements? When will they arrive?

60070116.text: Yeah... That's what he said he was gonna do, anyway.

60070117.text: Hmm... He hasn't contacted me about that yet. As per standing orders, he should be leading a team to root out the Wild Hunt, but I haven't received any reports for a while now.

60070118.text: *sigh* Well, he does act outside the remit of his orders sometimes. I'm his superior, yes, but I wouldn't say I have much control over his actions.

60070119.text: So he made the call for backup on his own initiative?

60070120.text: Hard to say. Contacting HQ's a tricky business. I should know, I've tried. They either refuse my requests outright, or end up dragging their feet.

60070121.text: And all the while, we're the ones who have to deal with the Wild Hunt — which, by the way, can strike anywhere in Nod-Krai without warning, sweeping across vast swathes of land. This has been a real test of our endurance, to say the least...

60070122.text: We need to send our personnel where they're needed most. A single missive will not do much to change HQ's attitude, I fear.

60070123.text: Flins understands this well enough, I'm sure.

60070124.text: (He sounds nice enough, but it feels like he's hiding something. This whole spiel sounds like a smokescreen.)

60070125.text: We usually sort our foes ahead of time into ones that our Ratniki will take care of, and ones that we'll target using the cannon.

60070126.text: I've finished the preliminary dispatch work already, but this cannon...

60070127.text: Okay, okay, okay! "Hurry up, Aino." "Fix this, Aino." You fix it if you're in such a hurry! That, or bring me some snacks. This is tiring work over here!

60070128.text: Ugh... Could you at least tell me how long we'll be delayed? We're way past our scheduled firing time.

60070129.text: Well that's your fault for firing too often recently! Machines get overworked too, you know? You could try thinking about their feelings for once, maybe?

60070131.text: In layman's terms, this refers to wear and tear. As such, a machine is more liable to fail the "unhappier" it becomes. The exact probability here would be...

60070132.text: Alright, alright. I'm not good at this stuff, I know that. But let me stress that we Lightkeepers are the primary financial backer of this cannon — and our backing does cover the fees for subsequent repair and maintenance.

60070133.text: Hmph. And I'd say that was a good deal for you! You should thank the Krumkake Craftshop — that means me, by the way — for making you such a huge and powerful weapon for such a measly price!

60070134.text: Do you even know how much it would've cost you if you'd bought all the parts legit and fresh off the assembly line?

60070135.text: Reminder: Your future snack budget will have to be halved without the long-term commission payment, Aino. Calculating: A viable and cheaper option... Lavender Melon Candy.

60070136.text: What? No! Absolutely not! I... L—Let me think, alright? It should take, maybe... three more hours?

60070137.text: Wouldn't this place be crawling with more monsters than there are Fungi in Sumeru by then!?

60070138.text: That might not be the concern you think it is. The monsters of the Wild Hunt are only active in the immediate vicinity of its attacks. They will not spread any further... on their own initiative, at least.

60070139.text: We Lightkeepers will also keep an eye on those areas, both to monitor the monsters and to prevent people from entering the cannon's blast radius.

60070140.text: That said... I'm afraid I can't wait three hours before dispatching manpower to the locations that the cannon won't be firing on.

60070141.text: And here's where my need for "manual labor" comes in. There are some checks I haven't finished yet, but with your help, I can get the repairs done sooner.

60070142.text: Wait, but we don't know a thing about this stuff. How much help will we be?

60070143.text: You'll be fine, trust me! Just take this — oh, and this.

60070144.text: Whoa, uh, this book is... so heavy... and what is this?

60070145.text: You can use this Beep-Boopitta to run diagnostics on the cannon. It'll tell you what to do. Oh, and this book will help you understand Beep-Boopitta.

60070146.text: This cannon was built using more than 50 components from different factories and manufacturers. Aino has bound the manuals into one volume. Also, please note: the device's name is "Birgitta."

60070147.text: S—So it's manuals all the way down, huh...

60070148.text: Yup. And if you're quick about this, we might just cut our time-to-fire down by a whole two thirds.

60070151.text: Nice! So, you'll check the outside, and Ineffa, inside. Come find me in the control room once you're done. Cool? Cool.

60070152.text: Instructions received. Please go about your work seriously as well, Aino. No snacking while I am away.

60070153.text: Hey! A little snacking will also improve my efficiency by two thirds!

60071901.text: Aino's explanations for things that don't interest her are a bit... "meh," aren't they? Or is that just how geniuses are?

60071902.text: Isn't Beep-Boopitta just following us around? Sure doesn't seem as smart as she said it is. How are we even supposed to know what to check?

60071905.text: I've watched Ineffa perform routine repairs before. It seems some sort of maintenance port must first be found, and then this small robot will automatically interface with it.

60071906.text: Ah, so you're in the know. Nice! What does that port look like?

60071907.text: Now that I'm not so sure of. Let's search around together and see what the robot reacts to.

60071909.text: Is this it? Hmm, probably not... Or this one? Oh, ew! Stinks of machine oil!

60071912.text: Hmm, that thing over there looks promising.

60071913.text: Where? Ooh, yeah, it does. Let's try it out.

60071914.text: Whoa! It's flying...! Does that mean we got it right?

60071915.text: So, uh... What do we do now?

60070201.text: Well, whaddya know? Aino was right. We got this working without understanding a thing Beep-Boopitta said!

60070202.text: Still, it's impressive how you figured things out right away.

60070205.text: Paimon's up next, along with this stupidly heavy book. Let's see... Should be just like checking a dictionary, right?

60070206.text: The matching result for this symbol is... "Check passed. All systems normal." Wait, is that it?

60070207.text: Well, as they say, "no news is good news."

60070208.text: Yeah, guess you're right. Just feels like we did all this stuff for nothing, that's all... On to the next spot, then.

60070209.text: Hehe, Paimon's getting the hang of this now. It's this thing, right?

60070211.text: And this time... Huh? Why are you angry? Oh... Huh, looks like its expressions are also prompts of a kind. Which page is that on...

60070212.text: We need to take note of the order in which its eye colors change — purple, red... Hey, slow down! Paimon didn't catch that!

60070214.text: Wha... So now we've got musical prompts too? Weren't you only supposed to be a "beep-boop" machine?

60070215.text: Alright, one final stop. This was quite a trip, huh?

60070216.text: Agreed. I must say, you two have a talent for maintenance work. A bit shaky at points, but not bad for your first job...

60070217.text: Heh, good eye! Paimon's the real deal when she deals for real, y'know!

60070218.text: Really, I'd have liked to share the load, but you were really getting into it, and I didn't want to interrupt.

60070219.text: Ugh, couldn't you have mentioned that earlier?

60070220.text: Anyway, let's get this all done in one go.

60070401.text: Hmm? Weren't you in a hurry to go check stuff?

60072002.text: What does that mean? Does the book say anything about it?

60072003.text: Hmm, a pictorial prompt this time... Don't worry, Paimon's just about gotten the hang of which prompts are listed where.

60072004.text: Uh, we gotta take note of the flashing patterns... "1 yellow flash, nothing for 2 seconds, then 2 yellow flashes" means... the components here are overdue for regular maintenance.

60072005.text: "Maintenance is a high-priority task. The device will be rendered inoperable until it is complete. Switch Beep-Boopitta to Input Mode to send out a signal to unlock components."

60072006.text: The description of Input Mode isn't on this page. Ugh, more page-flipping...

60072007.text: After more page-flipping, then even more page-flipping, Paimon manages to adjust the little robot as instructed.

60072008.text: Phew, that was a real struggle... Well, Paimon needs a break now.

60072010.text: Good work indeed. But it seems this Input Mode requires some additional work to operate.

60070501.text: Checking snack stock... Lower than expected. Please explain, Aino.

60070502.text: Later, later! Can't you see I'm busy... Y'know, saving the poor, anxious inhabitants of this town?

60070601.text: Looks like we're all good. We can remove this thing now.

60070603.text: No clue, frankly. But whatever — I got a feeling we've all given up trying to figure this cannon out.

60070604.text: I'll go get the replacement component. We should be done once we pop it in here.

60070605.text: What do you think? Maintenance work's easier than running errands, wouldn't you say?

60070606.text: Hehe, that's for sure. We're counting on you, Sousi!

60070607.text: Y'know what? Paimon took him for the stony type at first, but he's actually a pretty nice guy.

60070608.text: Let's wait for him here, huh?

60070610.text: Yep. Sousi's gone to get the replacement component — we'll be done here once we put it on.

60070611.text: Allow me to check against the recorded data... Yes. This component is approaching its replacement deadline.

60070612.text: The cannon will generate immense recoil when fired. If this is not controlled, the firing platform will become misaligned. This part is designed to anchor the cannon and ensure accuracy when aiming.

60070613.text: Huh. So if the cannon isn't fixed in place... will it start spinning around like some kind of massive firework?

60070614.text: A novel analogy... but an apt one. The large-scale damage that might follow would be undesirable by anybody's standards.

60070615.text: This component is currently easily damaged. The materials are not up to par, and there are still some design flaws. But Aino and I are working to improve it.

60070616.text: Estimated waiting time remaining: 7 minutes. Would you like a krumkake?

60070617.text: Yay! Dessert's just the best after a hard day's work!

60070618.text: Certainly. It will be ready shortly.

60070620.text: Observation: Freshly-baked krumkake results in the most efficient improvements upon human happiness indices. As such, I activated an internal heater before starting repairs.

60070621.text: Hehe, thanks for the treat! Aino's lucky to have you.

60070623.text: Sure enough, Sousi returns seven minutes later on the dot. You finish installing the spare part before returning to the control room.

60070624.text: Thanks! Things went great over here too. So, as we agreed, I'll have the cannon up and firing in no time!

60070625.text: Understood. I will inform the inhabitants of Nasha Town and have them make preparations for the shock and noise that will inevitably ensue.

60070626.text: And I will inform the Ratniki stationed around Wild Hunt anomalies to make sure they fall back in a timely fashion.

60070627.text: Thanks for your kind assistance. I'd better make a move — Ratniki from other sites should have sent reports back here, and I'll need to sort them out promptly.

60070629.text: Bet this huge cannon's a real sight when it fires.

60070630.text: That is correct. A huge crowd tends to gather on its own accord on such occasions.

60070631.text: Pure, bright energy rays have never failed to inspire obsessed admirers. If you are interested, you can come back later to behold it in all of its glory.

60070632.text: #Sure. We did help fix it, after all, {NICKNAME}. It'd be weird if we didn't want to see it in action.

60070635.text: Oh, yeah. Wonder where that strange phantom went, never mind what it's doing...

60070636.text: Let's try our luck at The Flagship. See you later, guys!

60070637.text: Heheh! Just be sure not to miss my masterpiece in action!

60071401.text: Is it just Paimon, or are there more people here now? Just as well, since we're sniffing for intel and all...

60071402.text: Might as well go in and ask around.

60071403.text: And maybe — just maybe — let's get some of their Berries and Fried Meat too, huh? We still haven't had it yet!

60071404.text: Ah, now you show your true motives.

60071406.text: Excuse me, are you guests? Ah, if you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.

60071407.text: Uh, no, we're not heading back to our room. Are we not allowed in here right now?

60071408.text: That is correct. Only those invited to the Banquet may enter. Our goal is to ensure that our regulars can enjoy peace of mind and comfort, so that they can speak freely with one another.

60071411.text: Haha. Familiar with our ways already, I see.

60071412.text: But here in Nod-Krai, "channels" hold equal value to Mora. I am but a lowly employee, so you'll have to forgive my inability to help in this matter.

60071413.text: It's fine. Can't be easy being you.

60071414.text: Hmm... Looks like we'll have to switch "channels," then...

60071415.text: And I know just the person.

60071416.text: Nefer, right? The Curatorium does seem to already have an amazing intel network up and running.

60071417.text: B—But if we ask her straight up, she'll likely squeeze us for all we're worth...

60070801.text: Hey Black Cat, we're here— Oh, it's you this time.

60070803.text: Not much, just here to say hi! Also, we'll be going to Hiisi Island later... so we can deliver the medicine to Lauma for you, if you need?

60070804.text: (How "thoughtful" of them... Bet they want something from me in return.)

60070805.text: Well... The faster the delivery, the better, naturally. And we're lacking free hands right now, so that would be a great help.

60070806.text: Jahoda's gone to get the medicine, and she should be back any moment now. If you have nothing else to do, feel free to wait here — I'll have someone bring you some snacks.

60070807.text: Don't mind if we do, then. Thanks!

60070810.text: Oh yes, I'm sure you've all heard about what's going on. Nasha Town's in turmoil, and right now, everyone wants intel — whether it's to strike it rich, save their lives, or escape whatever predicament they've found themselves in.

60070811.text: Ah, so you're busy making Mora. How nice...

60070812.text: It's not all good news, I'm afraid. We're stretched so thin that our clients have taken to competing for our services via "auction."

60070813.text: The price for taking priority slots has all but skyrocketed... In other words, we've had to suspend "free" intel handouts for now.

60070814.text: (She...! Ugh, she cornered us right away. Did she guess what we really wanted from the start?)

60070815.text: Is there anything we can do for you, then?

60070816.text: *sigh* If there's anything that worries me right now, it's the Wild Hunt. It affects everything we do, yet the number of people who can ensure "cargo safety" in the face of such a threat is vanishingly small.

60070817.text: Hmm? That doesn't sound too hard. If you need something delivered, hit us up and consider it sent!

60070818.text: Is that so? But... Ah, no, no, forget I said anything. I mean, you're great heroes. How could I waste your precious time on trifles like these?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to The Flagship once again

60072601.text: Lady Nefer, a pleasure to see you. Oh? And our guests from earlier, I see.

60072602.text: That's right. My apologies, consider it my fault for not having explained the Banquet's rules to them beforehand.

60072603.text: Oh, no, it was no trouble at all. Please, do come in.

60072605.text: (Not even an invitation check? Paimon didn't realize Nefer was such a big shot... Guess "channels" really do take you places.)

subQuests.subQuestName: Mingle with the crowd and wait for an opportunity to act

60070901.text: After you enter, Nefer brings you and Paimon to a spot near the bar before walking into an inner room to talk business with The Flagship's manager.

60070902.text: As you wait, you notice that everyone seems wary of the two of you, and the volume of the chatter lowers significantly.

60070903.text: This stifling atmosphere persists until Nefer returns...

60070905.text: Pardon me. I'm sure we're all having a good time, but I would like you all to meet a mysterious guest I invited for just this occasion.

60070906.text: I give you tonight's special guest, a renowned mixologist from Mondstadt!

60070908.text: Ladies and gentlemen, it is an honor.

60070910.text: I'm sure that no more needs to be said about Mondstadt's wine industry — after all, we are all connoisseurs of fine drink here.

60070911.text: The special drinks menu is being set before you as we speak. Now then, for a time, let us set aside our worries and enjoy these exotic spirits from afar.

60070912.text: Ah, I see. A new face for the bar.

60070913.text: And here I was thinkin', "that ain't a familiar face." No wonder...

60070914.text: Well, it's a rare occasion to be sure. Wanna order a glass or two?

60070916.text: I spoke to the owner. The bar is all yours.

60070917.text: The recipes are available for your perusal here. Not to worry, I've taken the liberty of removing the more... challenging options.

60070918.text: I guess we'll just have to give this a shot.

60070919.text: Previous experience coming in handy. Who'd have thought it...

60070920.text: How'd you set this all up so quickly?

60070921.text: Well, as long as you know what both sides need, negotiations are essentially just a process of confirming the deal. No one would turn a beneficial offer down now, would they?

60070922.text: The Flagship already had plans to invite a professional mixologist from Mondstadt anyway — so consider this a trial run, with the list of drinks brought out in advance.

60070923.text: Demyan will assist you. Serving guests with drinks will be the perfect opportunity for you.

60070924.text: Of course, every guest will have their quirks, so you'll have to be careful not to arouse their suspicions.

60070925.text: Got it. We'll give it a try.

60070926.text: In the meantime, I'll go mingle with some of the guests who... pique my interest. There'll be a little event during the Banquet's second half, by the way. See you then.

subQuests.subQuestName: Deliver the drinks to the guests
Take the opportunity to gather intel
Deliver the drink to the guest

60072201.text: W—Wait. What are you angling for, exactly?

subQuests.subQuestName: Take the opportunity to gather intel

60072301.text: Though the truth has been revealed, our deep connection with the moon remains unchanged — in fact, its power runs in our very veins...

60072302.text: What has changed is our understanding — of where the true moon lies, and that we must walk our own path in life without relying on a power outside of ourselves.

60072303.text: Which is why we now say: Come night or day, may the moonlight connect us.

subQuests.subQuestName: Take the opportunity to gather intel
Find a place to be discreet and keep gathering intel
Deliver the drink to the guest

60071001.text: Oh, so this order was yours, huh?

60071004.text: Ah, you two must be Nefer's friends. A pleasure to meet you. If you've got a moment, let's have a drink — on my tab, of course.

60071005.text: Paimon doesn't recall there being any other orders right now. Sure then, we can take a break.

60071006.text: Haha. Then come, sit! Demyan, two Wildberry Trails, if you would — without alcohol. Much obliged!

60071007.text: Hintsa's the name. I help out at the Rossum Workshop in town — they usually put me in charge of making and repairing simple machines.

60071008.text: Paimon's name is Paimon. Pleased to meet'cha!

60071013.text: ...Anyway, help me keep an eye out, alright? Valuable intel will be suitably compensated.

60071014.text: Oh, come on, is that how it is between us? I mean, I wouldn't even have this job if it hadn't been for your help back then.

60071015.text: So you've known each other a long time?

60071016.text: That's right. I came to Nod-Krai with nothing at all. Would've starved on the streets if I hadn't met Nefer.

60071017.text: She lent me money to study a craft, and even introduced me to Aino and the Voynich Guild, which is how I slowly carved out a living for myself.

60071018.text: That's... Yeah, that's a huge favor.

60071019.text: Huh, so Nefer can be a nice person sometimes huh?

60071020.text: Haha! Well, I'd also say she needed a willing and able machinist at her disposal.

60071021.text: Wait, don't we already have Aino for that?

60071022.text: Come now, Aino's talents are better spent on issues bigger than basic machine repair and component manufacture.

60071023.text: I did think myself a dab hand at such work at first, but compared to her, I might as well be a trainee who couldn't weld a wire to save his life. Got the scoldings to show for it, too.

60071024.text: It took me a long while, but I finally got to the point where I could make my own machines and even maintain some of Aino's relatively complex ones, like kuuvahki detectors or mechanical arms.

60071025.text: He's the one responsible for maintaining Jahoda's robotic arm.

60071026.text: Ooh, speaking of that, didn't Sousi have a mechanical arm too?

60071027.text: That's right, one of Aino's masterful designs. I could never design one of those in my life, but if you gave me its blueprint, I could hammer one out.

60071028.text: Nowadays, I've got regular customers, which makes for a decent keep. Even got a kid, if you can believe it — I wouldn't have, had you told me my future when I first arrived here.

60071029.text: On the flipside, being a family man means I can't just flee this place whenever I feel like it... so I'm afraid I'm counting on you to help solve this Wild Hunt crisis.

60071030.text: All the more reason to be proactive and do your part. Wringing our hands in despair does us no good in times of crisis.

60071031.text: Oh, wait. Just another question that's been bothering me. Have you heard anything about people seeing illusions within Wild Hunt anomalies? People they know, perhaps?

60071032.text: Hmm. I have heard of humanoid shapes being sighted, but familiar faces... No.

60071033.text: Most would think they'd lost their wits from fright if they started hallucinating. After all, no ordinary person could survive an assault from those monsters.

60071034.text: Does this have anything to do with our current Wild Hunt crisis?

60071036.text: Ah, alright, I get it. I'll keep my ear to the ground for you — and naturally, my lips will stay tightly sealed.

60071037.text: Then we'll take our leave. Enjoy your drinks.

60071038.text: He's a social man. You can often find him here chatting with friends, and he's had contact with all manner of clients.

60071039.text: Since he's never heard of the Wild Hunt exhibiting the power to imitate familiar faces, might it be safe to assume that our phantom wants to keep that a secret?

60071040.text: Huh, that does sound worth noting... How about we go talk to a few more people?

60071041.text: A good idea, and one our upcoming activity will facilitate. Let me show you how it's done.

60071011.text: Ah yes, I've heard. Lots of knights over there in Mondstadt. I imagine your title's an impressive one back home, huh?

60071012.text: Um, w—we were just messing with you there...

subQuests.subQuestName: Return to the counter and take part in the activity

60071201.text: Thank you for waiting, everyone. The Roulette Showdown is ready to begin.

60071203.text: C'mon, let's go try our hand.

60071206.text: Haha, no you won't. The one who'll be mixing the Roulette Special has to take part — those are the rules.

60071208.text: (There's Nefer's hand-signal again. Let's go with it.)

60071211.text: Since we have a new friend with us today, let me go over the rules in brief.

60071212.text: The wheel before you is divided into an inner and outer circle. Participants must take turns to spin the pointer of the inner circle. Whatever beverage it stops at, our lucky contestant will drink.

60071213.text: The drinks are divided into juice, tea, and alcohol, with that last further divided into three levels by intensity.

60071214.text: Spin your way to a non-alcoholic beverage, and you'll score no points. Otherwise, you get 1 to 3 based on alcohol content.

60071215.text: During a round of drinking, one participant may choose another with less points than them, and pose a question, which the other party must then answer.

60071216.text: This sounds like it might favor those who score higher, but push your luck, and you might not recall any answers you were given the next day. Defeats the purpose, wouldn't you say?

60071217.text: And that's why the person mixing the drinks has to take part. Y'know, just in case they decide to pour heavy, then sit back and watch the show.

60071218.text: (Not that our newcomer looks like the drinking type. Either way, looks like we're in for a show.)

60071219.text: Anything you drink will be replenished — and additionally, I have decided to sponsor a "grand prize" for this grand occasion...

60071221.text: What? Do my ears deceive me? A chance to drink "Dark Horse" in Nod-Krai?

60071222.text: "Dark Horse," eh... Guess we'll have to take part now, huh?

60071223.text: Hehe... Indeed, the "Dark Horse" could be yours to enjoy, so long as your luck holds — and so long as you can remember its taste the day after.

60071224.text: And if our lucky winner can drain the whole serving in one go, they will gain the right to ask everyone a question, regardless of their score.

60071225.text: High-risk, high-reward... That's gotta be some strong alcohol.

60071226.text: Now, if there are no other questions, let us begin. Allow me to get the ball rolling.

60071227.text: Intensity 3? Looks like I'll have to put my back into it today.

60071230.text: My turn, my turn! Alright, man, 'fess up. You've been making a killing lately — where's it all been coming from?

60071231.text: Hey, bro, I heard you met up with some big shot from the Voynich Guild! Mind introducing me sometime?

60071232.text: Tch... A normal drink, huh? Must be my lucky day.

60071233.text: We've reached the final round of the Roulette Showdown. Let's see who gets the last laugh.

60071234.text: Gotta shay, you Mondstadters really know your alrcohol... Those rrecipes are... superr good... teash me, would ya...

60071235.text: Hahah, I wuz wantin' to ask 'bout yer waif... Err, your wife...

60071236.text: (I've rolled non-alcoholic drinks without fail the last few rounds. This zero-point game is no accident...)

60071237.text: (Similarly, Nefer's been maintaining an ever-so-slight lead, and has been using it to ask ever-so-slightly probing questions. That can't just be luck.)

60071238.text: (I can tell that Dobrawa was lucky enough to survive stumbling into a Wild Hunt. But Nefer's turn is...)

60071242.text: Whooooa! Newface here just drew the "Dark Horse"!

60071245.text: #H—Hey. Will you be alright, {NICKNAME}? You wanna just give this one to Paimon?

60071246.text: #Whoa, {M#he}{F#she} actually downed it in one gulp!

60071247.text: Nice job! No wonder you Mondstadters have such a reputation!

60071248.text: What did you see while you were inside the Wild Hunt anomaly?

60071249.text: Me? Well, what do you think? Monsters, of course!

60071251.text: Absolutely. If there was something else, I didn't stop to see it. Just took off as fast as I could...

60071252.text: Oh, and guess who showed up just as I'd gotten out of there? Those good-for-nothin' Ratniki, that's who.

60071253.text: If my luck had been just a little worse, they'd have found nothing but my corpse — or whatever was left of it, anyway.

60071254.text: ...Either way, there's nothing in there you'd want to see.

60071255.text: (Even those who have had a personal encounter with the Wild Hunt know nothing about the strange phantom we saw. It seems Nefer's judgment was on point.)

60071256.text: I see some downcast faces. Why, have we all hit our limit?

60071257.text: Says who? I'm still raring to go!

60071258.text: Cuz you... din' drink... Dat mush...

60071259.text: Hehe, in that case, let me raise another glass — to a blast of a Showdown, and a wonderful evening.

60071101.text: Hmm? Are they playing cards? Paimon spies some Elemental Dice...

60071102.text: Same as usual, then? One die, 100,000 Mora.

60071103.text: I'm not here to do business with you...

60071104.text: Come now, I've already ordered us drinks. Or are you looking to add another line to your ledger of arrears?

60071106.text: O—Oh, so this is a business deal?

60071107.text: So, let's go over this again. One die, 100,000 Mora.

60071112.text: Hehe, then we have a deal. Come, you two, take a seat as well.

60071113.text: *sigh* What are we even doing here?

60071114.text: I can give you three things: The features of the Wild Hunt, the exact locations where it has appeared, and the intel we've received from the Lightkeepers.

60071115.text: The Wild Hunt is in fact a phenomenon linked to Abyssal power. Fog and monsters follow in its wake, posing a lethal danger to ordinary people.

60071116.text: On the flipside, these monsters cannot leave the fog, so the disaster cannot spread quickly—

60071118.text: *sigh* Fair enough. Then I won't beat around the bush.

60071119.text: Here's a map of current Wild Hunt anomalies that I snagged from the Lightkeepers, including the locations they'll soon be bombarding.

60071121.text: We've never seen anything like this either. That's why everyone's so worked up.

60071123.text: Cool it, alright? I'm not done...

60071124.text: Now, the Lightkeepers don't want you to know this, but weirdly enough, more Wild Hunt sites have disappeared than their involvement would indicate.

60071125.text: Isn't that normal? They're not the only ones fighting the Wild Hunt, after all. Adventurers do that too... and maybe some just go poof by themselves?

60071126.text: I'd agree. And really, we've always had a small, stable discrepancy between reported anti-Wild Hunt ops and anomalies cleared. That variance... has become a gulf lately.

60071128.text: I've got two theories. One, that some new force is clearing the Wild Hunt out in secret... or two, that some Ratniki are not reporting the work they do on purpose.

60071129.text: The odds of the former happening is low. Not many organizations can even engage the Wild Hunt, never mind keep those operations a secret.

60071130.text: If you're interested, I'd recommend following the latter train of thought.

60071131.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't really get it... What would anyone gain from doing that?

60071132.text: Let's just note it down first.

60071133.text: Now that's what I call interesting intel. No wonder you've been doing well for yourself lately — even if you've mostly just been reselling my intel.

60071134.text: Please... stop. This is all I've got for you.

60071135.text: Oh, stop that. Why, people might start thinking me a bully.

60071136.text: Let me give you an opportunity, instead — out of respect for your independent intelligence-gathering. An answer to a simple question, for 50,000 off your debt.

60071137.text: Have you heard of people seeing familiar faces within a Wild Hunt anomaly, or experiencing something akin to, say, an illusion?

60071138.text: No, nothing like that. Nothing at all but ghostly shadows...

60071139.text: Nothing at all, hmm? Not even for 50,000 Mora? Either you don't take your debt seriously, or you're confident you can pay it off...

60071140.text: H—Hey, no means no, alright? This is about my dignity as an intel broker — Mora doesn't factor in here at all.

60071141.text: Okay, well that puts me at ease.

60071142.text: Ugh, you really are the same as ever...

60071143.text: And you've learned quite well. Go on, then. I'll swing by again — sometime soon, perhaps.

60071146.text: Indeed I am. He's resold my intel quite a few times now, pocketing the difference afterwards. Rather dishonest dealing, if I may say so.

60071147.text: As luck would have it, he would only purchase information from me when he was just about done negotiating with his buyer, so I arranged a little something just for him. A painful lesson, you might call it.

60071149.text: Oh, I was downright beneficent in charging for that betrayal. It was more about the message, really.

60071150.text: Good thing we're on the same team...

60071151.text: In any case, I believe that's all we'll get here. Let's go through what we've learned outside.

subQuests.subQuestName: Analyze the information you have with Nefer

60071301.text: Most of our intel seems quite dispersed, so let's try piecing it all together.

60071302.text: Well... First, no one else has seen that weird phantom, apart from our encounter on Starsand Shoal.

60071303.text: Indeed. And we have that from multiple accounts, so each statement corroborates the others.

60071304.text: What in Teyvat could that phantom be planning...?

60071305.text: The Wild Hunt anomaly that occurred at Starsand Shoal seems quite unique.

60071306.text: Agreed. Instances of the Wild Hunt afflicting Nod-Krai in general have increased in frequency, but the phenomenon itself hasn't changed much.

60071307.text: What you encountered must have been something special, with our mastermind concealing themselves within... in order to target the Moon Marrow.

60071308.text: In which case, two questions arise: Who is this mastermind? And why would they want the Moon Marrow?

60071309.text: (Additionally, that intel broker mentioned that some Lightkeepers might be withholding information. Given the inconsistencies in Flins's words and deeds, he might be a likely suspect...)

60071310.text: (But... let's not share that with Nefer for now.)

60071311.text: I'll continue investigating along these two lines. We can reconvene again if any progress is m—

60071313.text: Luckily, the store owner kept the medicine bottle I left on the table safe for me. Here you go!

60071314.text: Thanks a bunch, Jahoda! Take a break, you've earned it.

60071315.text: Oh no, I've got work to do later, and anyway, isn't the cannon about to go off?

60071316.text: I was watching it the whole way back, praying it wouldn't fire — not until I got back, y'know? Again, lucky me.

60071317.text: Huh, so you're interested in that big gun?

60071318.text: Of course! I mean, just think about it. Something that size is bound to be comprised of thousands, even tens of thousands of parts, fused in such a way that it can operate smoothly and fire off a super-giant, super-strong beam!

60071319.text: Isn't that just so cool— I mean, miraculous? Like, a miracle created through countless careful calculations?

60071320.text: Mmm. It has been a while since the last time it fired. Go on, feel free to go watch. Work can wait — for a while.

60071321.text: Ah, thanks, Boss! Anyway, y'all wanna come? It'll be worth the while and worth your wait, I swear!

60071322.text: Eh, might as well. Fruits of our labor and everything, y'know?

60071326.text: Wow, what a crowd! People seem pretty excited, too. Just goes to show how big a deal this cannon is, huh?

60071327.text: Oh, for sure! One shot, one kill — problems solved! Simple and practical, just the way we like it.

60071328.text: And even if that wasn't how it worked, just listen to how it roars! If that isn't "power," I don't know what is...

60071329.text: If only I had that kinda strength...

60071330.text: Hey, don't think like that! Your skills and smarts have been a big help to us too!

60071331.text: (R—Really? They think that? Ohh... I'll do my best next time we work together, for sure!)

60071335.text: Finally, all fixed up. Nothing to fear now, hahaha!

60071336.text: Hehe, awesome. Felt that one in my bones!

60071337.text: Whew... That sure was powerful... and pretty dazzling, too! Guess that's why everyone's been counting on this thing. Surely the Wild Hunt doesn't stand a chance!

60070301.text: Apologies. If you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.

60070702.text: Good work. Now then, get the drink to the guest — wouldn't want to keep them waiting.

60070703.text: Hmm, that didn't come out quite right. Let's try again, shall we?

60073401.text: Ah, guests invited by Nefer, then? Welcome to The Flagship.

60079902.text: Huh. Would I be killing myself with fright here if that was an option?

60079904.text: Tell you what. I envy people like you. I'm like a man in a leaking boat — soon to be food for the fish.

60079905.text: I wouldn't have come to this dump if there were any better place to be.

60079906.text: Come now, surely it isn't that bad. We've still got the Lightkeepers.

60079907.text: Heh. You trust 'em? I wouldn't. Wouldn't trust anyone, really. We're stuck with the Wild Hunt here. The Snezhnayans can't be bothered, the Lightkeepers can't spare the people... And everyone else? They're a mess.

60079908.text: I'd sooner put an ounce of faith in that cannon...

60079909.text: Forget it. Let's just drink. Let's see if this new mixologist is worth the billing.

60079910.text: Excuse me... Do you need anything else?

60079911.text: I doubt the Snezhnayans will stand idly by if this Wild Hunt problem gets any worse.

60079912.text: I wouldn't be so sure. Do they look like they give a hoot about anything other than their precious research?

60079915.text: Bet you some people are just waiting for this place to fall further into chaos...

60079916.text: You've got a plan for that, then?

60079917.text: Hard to say. But what I can say is that the situation in Nasha Town will get out of hand if that cannon isn't fired soon.

60079918.text: That gun's a symbol — the most solid proof that ordinary folks like us can stand up against the Wild Hunt.

60079919.text: W—Wait. What are you angling for, exactly?

60079920.text: Well, what if that was nothing but an illusion? What if, let's say, the cannon was never meant to be fired, for our sakes at least?

60079921.text: ...Surely this town is still of value to those who control it?

60079922.text: Of course, of course. But that's all it is. Value. For us, though, there's no place but Nasha Town — and we're putting its life, and ours, in their hands.

60079923.text: I get what you mean... *sigh* Let's just see how this plays out first.

60079924.text: Seems like they're all talking about the cannon already. Guess that's why Sousi was so anxious...

60079926.text: You sure your business is more important than your life...

60079927.text: *sigh* I'll lose money at this rate...

60079929.text: Might as well drink our fill today...

60079931.text: After you enter, Nefer brings you and Paimon to a spot near the bar before walking into an inner room to talk business with The Flagship's manager.
